No figure is added, dropped or reordered, and every source the earlier body cited is still cited unless this review names the source that replaced it and why. The earlier bytes stand in for the live article only while the live article is exactly the reviewed successor, so older reviews, runs and receipts that pinned the earlier bytes still check the bytes they recorded.

edits.before: The claim: keep the architecture general, scale data and parameters, and generalist robot intelligence follows, as it did for language. Rich Sutton's 2019 essay The Bitter Lesson frames it: general methods that leverage computation win in the long run <Cite id="sutton-bitter-lesson-2019" />. Brooks answered six days later, in a reply that paraphrases Sutton and describes itself, including its closing comment, as "seventy six words shorter than Sutton’s post" <Cite id="brooks-better-lesson-2019" />. edits.before: The claim is that a learned model of how the world evolves can replace most real-robot data: plan in it, or train the policy inside it. NVIDIA's Cosmos 3 and Meta's V-JEPA 2 are the largest such bets ([what is a world model?](/world-models/taxonomy/)). V-JEPA 2 plans zero-shot reaching, grasping and pick-and-place on Franka arms in unseen labs after post-training on less than 62 hours of unlabeled robot video <Cite id="vjepa2-2025" />. DreamZero, a world action model that serves as the policy, reports over 2x better generalization to new tasks and environments than state-of-the-art VLAs <Cite id="dreamzero-2026" /> ([generative video](/world-models/generative-video/)).

edits.before: Dexterity is solved when one policy does Holson's fifteen tasks in unseen homes at human-competent speed, with no per-task data and with published success rates. Nobody is close: the best public scoreboard is about half success with per-task training. The open question is which data closes the gap. If Tesla or Figure reach household dexterity from video at scale, the tactile gap was a transitional hardware shortage.
edits.after: Dexterity is solved when one policy does Holson's fifteen tasks in unseen homes within ten times Holson's own time, with no per-task data and with published success rates <Cite id="holson-olympics-2025" />. Nobody is close: the best public scoreboard is about half success with per-task training <Cite id="pi-olympics-2025" />. The open question is which data closes the gap. If Tesla or Figure reach household dexterity from video at scale, the tactile gap was a transitional hardware shortage <Cite id="brooks-dexterity-2025" /> <Cite id="figure-go-big-2025" />.

edits.before: The robot-specific layer splits liability in two. ISO 10218-1 covers the robot as partly completed machinery, the manufacturer's obligation; ISO 10218-2 covers the application and its cell, the integrator's <Cite id="iso-10218-1-2025" /> <Cite id="iso-10218-2-2025" />. Both were republished in February 2025 at editions 3 and 2, the first major revision since 2011. The US adoption, ANSI/A3 R15.06-2025, added a Part 3 on user requirements in October 2025 <Cite id="rr-ansi-r1506-2026" />.
edits.after: The robot-specific layer splits liability in two. ISO 10218-1 covers the robot as partly completed machinery, the manufacturer's obligation; ISO 10218-2 covers the application and its cell, the integrator's <Cite id="iso-10218-1-2025" /> <Cite id="iso-10218-2-2025" />. Both were republished in February 2025 at editions 3 and 2, the first major revision since 2011.
